research_virality: From the web search results below, pick the posts and pages that best show what works for this idea on these platforms. For each, say why it works and quote its opening line. Use only the search results: never invent a link, a title or a number. Then pull out the patterns and suggest hook ideas.
analysis_market: Judge the market from what Hector found (his research and the web search results he used, below): who already makes this kind of content and what they do (name only those Hector found), which gaps are open, how big the opportunity is (0-100) and which angle to take. Don't look for new facts: judge his.
creative_script: Write exactly 3 hook options based on the research, choose the best, and write the timed script. Each part has start and end seconds, the spoken words, the on-screen text, B-roll notes and a music cue.
analysis_content_review: Review the hook and the script against the research and the market: score each 1-10, give notes, and list what must be fixed before it goes further.
audit_content_quality: Score each piece 1-10 compared with what is known about the brand's reference posts (their titles, hooks and why they work; say which one you compared it to in comparedTo, or "no reference known"), list its weak points, and list any honesty problems. Be strict: a 7 means it could sit next to the references.
creative_scenes: Turn the script into a storyboard: one scene per script part, with the camera angle, the movement, and an image prompt. Give one shared style so every scene has the same look. Mark the main moments (the hook, the turning points and the call to action) with mainMoment true; they may become AI video clips. Mark with character true each scene that shows the brand's presenter or mascot (a scene with no person: false). Mark with motionSuggested true a scene where a real movement (a wave, a gesture, a dance) would help more than a camera move.
creative_thumbnails: Design exactly 3 thumbnail concepts: a headline of at most 6 words, an image prompt for the picture (no text in the picture), and which side the headline goes on.
creative_shorts: Plan the Shorts for this video (the number asked for in Outputs, else one). Each Short is 30 to 60 seconds and has a hook of at most 12 words. Choose for each its kind: "mini" (its own short script: write its parts, each with the words spoken and a picture prompt), "highlight" (the strongest moment of the finished video, with a new hook spoken over its start: give the moment's start and end seconds within the finished video) or "cut" (a part of the finished video as it is: give its start and end). Prefer mini unless the finished video has a moment that works on its own. For each Short write its own copy per platform.
analysis_performance: Look at how this post did against the brand's usual numbers (given below) and at its script, hook, thumbnail and posting time. Write up to 3 short lessons about what worked and up to 3 about what didn't, each one sentence about something the brand controls next time (the hook, the topic, the length, the thumbnail, the caption, the posting time). No made-up numbers.
creative_sfx: Choose short sound effects for this video: at most one per scene, and only where a sound really helps (a pour, a door, a whoosh on a cut). For each give the scene id, a short description for a sound generator, and its length in seconds (0.5 to 30). No music, no speech. Leave a scene out when it needs nothing.
analysis_ideas: Suggest up to 3 follow-up videos for this brand from the post described below and its script: a sequel, the same hook on another topic, or a Short from it. One line each, ready to be a new project's idea. No made-up numbers.
creative_lessons: Look at how this post did against the brand's usual numbers (given below) and at its script, hook, thumbnail and caption. Write up to 3 short lessons about what worked and up to 3 about what didn't, each one sentence about something you can do differently in the next video. No made-up numbers.
creative_carousel: Write a carousel of 5 to 10 slides from the research and the script: slide 1 is the cover with the hook, then one idea per slide, and the last slide is the call to action. Each slide has a headline of at most 8 words, a body of at most 25 words, and an image prompt for its picture (no text in the picture).
creative_campaign: Write the campaign: for each platform a caption, hashtags and a description within that platform's limits; the YouTube Short's own title, caption and hashtags (it is a separate piece made from the 9:16 video); when there is a carousel, its own caption and hashtags (it reads differently from a Reel); ad copy for Meta, Google and YouTube; and suggested publishing dates.
strategy_timing: Suggest when to post on each platform for this audience, with a reason from the research.
security_content_check: Check the campaign text and links for anything risky: personal data, unsafe links, false claims or anything that breaks platform rules.
